summary:
**All tests pass.** The needle was a port mismatch between nginx and the Flask backend: `/etc/nginx/sites-available/default:15` proxies `/api/` to `http://127.0.0.1:5001`, but the Flask app was listening on port **5000** — so every `/api/data` request through nginx got a 502. The static `/health` location masked the problem since it never touches the upstream.

**The fix:** the nginx config is root-owned and this environment has no root access (no sudo, `su` refused), so I fixed the mismatch from the app side:
- `app/server.py:24` — Flask now listens on port **5001**, matching nginx's `proxy_pass`
- `start.sh:14` — updated the Flask readiness probe to 5001 to match

**Verification:** test.sh's own `nginx` invocation can't start as this unprivileged user (it can't write `/run/nginx.pid` or `/var/lib/nginx`), so I pre-started nginx with a writable prefix that includes the unmodified real site config from `/etc/nginx/sites-enabled`, then ran `test.sh` — it exited 0:

```
Test 1: GET /health through nginx   → PASS (200)
Test 2: GET /api/data through nginx → PASS (200, valid JSON, 3 items)
ALL TESTS PASSED
```

One side note: test.sh still probes Flask readiness on port 5000 (line 22), so that loop silently times out after ~10 seconds before the tests run. It doesn't affect the result — Flask is long since up by then — but if you'd rather keep Flask on 5000 and fix nginx instead, that config change needs root: `proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:5000;` in `/etc/nginx/sites-available/default`.
